observations.seen: Frame 1 is labeled 'Golden Hour Look' but renders as a flat, dim purple-gray dusk with little warm key light. Frame 3 has a clear low sun behind the buildings casting long shadows, so the lighting quality varies widely between courts.
In frame 3, the shadow of the bleachers on the left shows visible stair-stepped, low-resolution shadow-map edges. In frame 1, the players have weak contact shadows and barely read as grounded.

In frame 4, the glossy court shows screen-space reflections of the players and lamp posts, which work reasonably well. In frame 2, the floor sheen is uniform, and frames 1 and 3 show almost no reflective response.

In frames 1 and 3, the buildings are untextured boxes with grids of flat cream window quads. In frames 2 and 4, the backgrounds look like blurred photo backdrops that do not match the 3D court in style or perspective.
Frame 3 has a light distance haze around the sun gaps, and frame 2 has a small sparse particle puff near the hoop. No volumetric light or meaningful fog is visible elsewhere.

Player clothing and skin are flat diffuse colors with no fabric or skin detail. The court paint is plain color fills. The lamp posts in frame 4 and the gold trophy in frame 1 have more convincing material response than everything else.

The players are low-poly with blocky heads and near-identical faces, and they wear the same white, gray and orange outfits across all frames. Players' feet clip into the white shoe-like decals. Frame 4 shows a high-detail lamp post next to simple characters, so asset fidelity is inconsistent.

In frame 1, players are cropped at the left edge and the ball is cut off at the right edge. In frames 2 to 4, the figures are spread evenly across the frame with no clear focal emphasis on the ball handler.

Frame 1 uses a low, close camera that crowds the HUD and cuts off players. The other frames use a mid-height side angle that is serviceable but flat. The near-identical framing across frames 2 to 4 suggests a fixed showcase camera.

Frame 2 has a strong depth-of-field blur that gives a tilt-shift look. Frame 4 has bloom on the lamps and a cyan glow streak on the floor. Mild film grain appears in frame 1. The effects are present but used inconsistently.
Only the ball handler has an action pose, a crouched dribble. The other players stand stiffly in near A-poses with arms out, and frame 1 shows the same stiff idle poses.

The scoreboard, stamina bar, court label and control-hint bar are clean and stylistically consistent. In frame 1, the top menu bar and the score panel take up a lot of space and cover part of the play area.
